title: Probabilistic preemptive admission with circuit-breaker integration and region-aware token budgeting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: During global spikes we observe correlated latency and error budget exhaustion in individual regions. Existing deterministic priority queues and hard admission gates either allow expensive tail-latency requests through (causing SLO burnout) or drop too much good traffic (high customer impact). Goal: design and implement a probabilistic preemptive admission controller that integrates with our circuit-breaker subsystem and enforces a region-aware token budget per tenant and route. The controller should: 1) allow soft degradation modes (probabilistic sampling, response reduction hints) when a region is under stress, 2) preempt long-running, low-value requests probabilistically rather than strictly by queue position, and 3) consult circuit-breaker state to avoid cascading retries across regions. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a canary rollout in two regions.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc with decision record merged in Confluence (link provided) and reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams
Prototype implementation in runtime that exposes a probabilistic admission policy flag and per-tenant region token buckets
Automated unit and integration tests covering token bucket refill, probabilistic preemption, and circuit-breaker interactions
Canary rollout in us-west1 and europe-west1 with telemetry dashboards showing expected degradation behavior
SLO validation: during a synthetic spike the 99p latency stays within 1.5x baseline for non-degraded tenants and error budget consumption for degraded tenants is limited to configured thresholds
Runbook entries updated and on-call training completed
discussion: 2026-03-10 - Aisha: Initial proposal drafted. Trade-offs considered: deterministic fairness vs utility-based probabilistic shedding. Leaning toward probabilistic preemption to preserve overall throughput while protecting tail latency.

2026-03-11 - Carlos: Runtime feasibility check complete. Kernel scheduling integration points identified (batch admission path + preemption hook). Concern: KV cache churn when evicting preempted requests. Action: add cache-awareness to preemption heuristic.

2026-03-12 - SRE review (Maya Li): Suggested region-aware token buckets tied to regional capacity and cross-region failover policy. Also requested a circuit-breaker signal channel to mark tenants as 'defer-to-secondary' to avoid client retries amplifying load.

2026-03-12 - Product review (Jonah Reed): Requested clear customer impact tiers and configuration knobs exposed via Console. Prefer default conservative settings for PLG users and aggressive options for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-13 - Design decision: Use a hybrid policy: base deterministic priority lanes for P0/P1 tenants + probabilistic preemption for P2/P3 and best-effort traffic. Token buckets operate per-tenant-per-region with an emergency spillover rate to other regions when network latency permits.

2026-03-14 - Implementation note (Carlos): Prototype branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1248. Added /admission/prob-preempt flag and metrics: admission_attempts, preempted_count, token_bucket_rejections, cb_deferred_count.

2026-03-14 - Ops comment (Irene Novak): Need dashboard tiles: per-region token utilization, tenant-level preemption rate, and cross-region reroute latency. Also add alert when preemption rate > 5% for 5m for top 20 tenants.

Open questions: How to set refill rates for new tenants? Do defaults come from historical QPS or tier? Should preemption probability be proportional to request token cost (estimated by sequence length)?
